axes.description: Which axes of `values` to blur along. `null` (default) blurs every axis. E.g. for a 2-D grid, `[0]` blurs only along axis 0, leaving axis 1 untouched. Negative indices count from the end, as in numpy.
axes.title: Axes

max_qubits.description: Safety cap on the total number of qubits `values`'s shape is allowed to require. A 1024x1024 2-D grid costs 20 qubits; a flat 1D list of up to 2**20 numbers also costs 20. Default 20, max 24.
max_qubits.title: Max Qubits

reach.description:
Controls how far from its original position a value can be affected by the blur:

- `0` — fully local: only neighbouring grid points are affected (default).
- `1` — fully non-local: any point on the grid can be affected equally.
reach.title: Reach

shots.description: If given, the grid is recovered from this many simulated projective measurements, introducing shot noise. If omitted (default), the exact (infinite-shot) probabilities are used.
shots.title: Shots

strength.description:
Strength of the effect, which controls the rotation applied to each qubit:

- `0` — the values are left unchanged.
- `1` — maximum blur.

A single number applies to every axis identically. A list applies per axis instead — one entry per axis in `axes` (or, if `axes` is omitted, one per axis of `values`) — so e.g. one axis can be left at `0` (untouched) while another is fully blurred.
strength.title: Strength

style.description: Quantum gate(s) used to apply the effect: any non-empty combination of the letters `x`, `y`, each selecting a rotation around that axis of the Bloch sphere (Rx/Ry). Every qubit gets the gates in `style` applied in order, left to right, all using the same angle for that qubit — e.g. `"xy"` applies Rx then Ry to each qubit, both by the same amount. `style` picks which gates run; `strength` (below) picks how hard, per axis.
style.title: Style

values.description: An arbitrarily nested list of non-negative numbers. The nesting depth is the grid's dimensionality: a flat list is 1-D, a list of lists is 2-D, etc. Must be rectangular (non-ragged).
values.title: Values

margin.description: Fraction of the active pitch span to pad above and below before blurring, giving the blur room to spread into adjacent pitches. `0` — no padding; blur is hard-clipped at the boundary notes. Default 0.15.
margin.title: Margin

mask.description: List of regions to blur, each as [track_index, start_seconds, end_seconds]. When omitted every note track is blurred in full. Tracks and time ranges not covered by the mask pass through unchanged. Example: [[1, 0.5, 2.0], [2, 1.0, 3.5]].
mask.title: Mask

qubits.description: Qubit budget per blur pass (4–20). Determines the largest piano-roll tile the quantum simulator handles in one shot; larger values avoid tiling but require more simulation memory. Default 20.
qubits.title: Qubits

reach.description:
Non-locality of the blur:

- `0` — fully local: only neighbouring pitches/times mix.
- `1` — fully non-local: any pitch can mix with any other.
reach.title: Reach

resolution.description: Number of MIDI ticks per piano-roll step (integer ≥ 0). `0` (default) — auto: uses the 5th-percentile note duration, robust to sequencer-artefact grace notes. Any positive value sets the step size directly; larger values produce a coarser grid and faster blur.
resolution.title: Resolution

threshold.description: Relative noise gate: a velocity delta must exceed threshold × max_velocity_in_roll to emit a note. Scales with the loudest note so it suppresses artefacts proportionally regardless of the overall dynamic level. Default 0.1.
threshold.title: Threshold

inputFiles.description: The image of your choice. The blur effect is applied RGB pixel values only, not the alpha channel. It means that if you submitted a PNG with transparent background, the background from the output will also be transparent.

inputFiles.name: mask
inputFiles.description:
Optional mask controlling where the effect is applied, on a per-pixel
basis. Must match the size of `image`. Each output pixel is a soft
blend `C = m · C_blurred + (1 - m) · C_original`, where `m` is the
normalised mask intensity at that pixel: black keeps the original,
white takes the fully blurred version, and grey values blend smoothly
between the two. Single-channel masks are used directly; RGB masks are
converted to luminance.

**Alpha-channel fallback**

If no mask is provided, the alpha channel of `image` is used instead
(transparent pixels keep the original, opaque pixels are blurred). For
RGB input with no alpha channel, the whole image is blurred.

absorption.description:
Fraction of the maximum absorption achievable at the given reflectance.

- `0` — no absorption.
- `1` — maximum absorption and minimum transmission.
absorption.title: Absorption

incoming_rays.description:
Number of light rays entering the stack simultaneously.

- Must be `>= layers` so that at least one ray is transmitted.
- Maximum enforced by the 21-qubit budget at validation time.
incoming_rays.title: Incoming Rays

interaction.description:
Strength of the nonlinear quantum interaction terms.

- `0` — interaction disabled; only reflectance and absorption shape the output.
- Positive vs. negative values of the same magnitude produce distinct colour patterns.
interaction.title: Interaction

layers.description:
Number of conducting sheets in the stack.

- Maximum enforced by the 21-qubit budget at validation time.
layers.title: Layers

reflectance.description:
Fraction of reflected power of a single ray and layer at normal incidence.

- `0` — perfect transmittance and no absorption.
- `1` — perfect mirror, no transmission or absorption.
reflectance.title: Reflectance

resolution.description:
Density of the angle–phase lookup table baked into the shader.

- Higher values reduce banding on close-up or oblique surfaces.
resolution.title: Resolution

style.description:
Selects which nonlinear interaction channels are active.

- `peaked` — reflection and transmission peak at the same angle for large number of layers.
- `frustrated` — competing interaction channels produce a non-monotone colour pattern.
- `3-body` — three-body interactions only; subtle, low-contrast effect.
- `constrained` — higher ray counts suppress transmission, deepening shadows.

allow_high_shots.description: Permit `shots` above 8192. Real hardware time scales linearly with shots, and emulated runs multiply shots by the number of data-qubit groups, so raising this can be expensive. Off by default.

backend_name.description: IBM device to target when mode='qpu', e.g. 'ibm_fez'. Required in that mode -- there is no least-busy auto-select. Ignored when mode='emu'.

discretize.description: Number of discrete levels to quantize `values` to. 0 encodes them continuously.

dynamic_range.description: Rescale the reconstruction to match a summary statistic of the original `values`, to counteract shot noise/decoherence shrinking its spread toward the middle of the range. 'none' leaves the reconstruction unchanged. 'min_max' rescales so its min and max match the input's. 'percentile' does the same using the 2nd/98th percentiles instead, less sensitive to outliers. 'mean_std' matches mean and standard deviation. 'abs_max' rescales by the single largest absolute value. 'min_avg_max' matches min, mean, and max all three at once.
dynamic_range.title: Dynamic Range

machine.description: Which emulator to use when mode='emu' (ignored when mode='qpu'). 'aer' is noiseless. 'fake_<chip>' options (e.g. 'fake_fez', 'fake_sherbrooke', 'fake_torino') are each calibrated to a real current IBM chip's noise.

shots.description: Number of measurement shots to sample. Capped at 8192 unless `allow_high_shots` is set; the hard ceiling is 32768. Note this is shots PER data-qubit group when mode='emu', not per run.

values.description: Array of floating-point values to encode. Either a flat list, a nested list of groups (one sublist per data-qubit group, in the exact order `list_groups(values, machine)` returns them), or that same shape written as a single string wrapped in [..] or (..), e.g. "[0.1,0.2,0.3]" for a flat list or "[[0.1,0.2],[0.3,0.4]]" / "([0.1,0.2],[0.3,0.4])" for groups. A group with more values than its capacity is rejected; a group with fewer is padded with zeros.

decay.description: Extra level roll-off per depth step, on top of |F|. 1.0 = none.
decay.title: Decay

depth.description: Echo depths t = 1..depth — the tap time slots.

emit.description: `audio` renders a WAV — your input processed, or the effect's own impulse response when no audio is supplied. `map` skips rendering entirely and returns only the time-mapped tap list, which is what a sequencer or a DAW plugin wants: same tap map, no audio work, no WAV to download.

exact.description: aer only: exact expectation values instead of sampling.
exact.title: Exact

feedback.description: Regeneration loop gain. The bus of selected taps is normalised first, so this is the fraction of signal that comes back round — always convergent, and 0.6 sounds like 0.6 on a rack unit rather than diverging.

feedback_source.description: Which taps regenerate. `kick`: only the kick site's column (the classic single regeneration tap). `all`: every tap.

ir_seconds.description: With no `audio` input, render the effect's own stereo impulse response for this long.

kick.description: Perturbation Pauli applied to the kick site between U and U†.
kick.title: Kick

kick_site.description: Regeneration source: the site that receives the impulse. Default: centre.
kick_site.title: Kick Site

lattice.description: Delay-line topology. `chain`: site → pan. `square` (Nighthawk-native): x → pan, y → diffusion.
lattice.title: Lattice

machine.description: Backend for the measurement: 'aer' (local, noiseless) or an IBM backend name such as 'ibm_phoenix'.

master_ms.description: Length of the master delay line in ms. One depth step = master_ms / depth. Ignored when bpm is set.
master_ms.title: Master Ms

min_level.description: |F| threshold below which a tap is dropped.
min_level.title: Min Level

n_sites.description: Chain length in qubits (= pan positions). Ignored for `square`.
n_sites.title: N Sites

negative_mode.description: What a negative F does. `invert`: flip polarity (phase-cancelling echo). `reverse`: play that tap's grains backwards. `phase`: rotate by arg(F) via a Hilbert transform — the only mode that uses F_im, so pair it with theta_z > 0.
negative_mode.title: Negative Mode

qpu_instance.description: IBM Quantum instance CRN. As with the token: required for `via: direct`, optional BYOK for `via: mothbackend`.
qpu_instance.title: Qpu Instance

qpu_token.description: IBM Quantum API token when machine is an IBM backend; falls back to QISKIT_IBM_TOKEN.
qpu_token.title: Qpu Token

ref_floor.description: |c_ref| below which a tap is dropped as unnormalisable. Default: 4/sqrt(shots), ~0 for exact simulation. Raise it to prune taps the noise floor cannot support.
ref_floor.title: Ref Floor

seed.description: RNG seed for the disorder realisation. Only audible when disorder > 0. Drawn as a 31-bit integer and returned in provenance if omitted. Capped at 2**53-1: above that, moth-api (Go) and any browser client re-spell the integer as a float64 and it stops matching the seed you sent.
seed.title: Seed

shots.description: Shots per circuit. Ignored when machine='aer' and exact=true. Above 8192 requires allow_high_shots.
shots.title: Shots

sr.description: Sample rate. Ignored when an `audio` file is supplied — that file's own rate is used.
sr.title: Sr

stereo_width.description: Scales the site → pan spread. 0 = mono.
stereo_width.title: Stereo Width

tail_ms.description: Silence appended to the input so the last tap and its regenerations fit. Default: computed from the tap map.
tail_ms.title: Tail Ms

theta_x.description: Transverse kick per layer (RX, rad) — the 'how quantum' dial. Low → loud regular taps; high → inverted, attenuated, erased.
theta_x.title: Theta X

theta_z.description: Phase layer (RZ, rad). 0 → real, two-signed taps. >0 → complex F, which `negative_mode: phase` renders as rotation.
theta_z.title: Theta Z

theta_zz.description: Coupling per layer (RZZ, rad). Non-monotonic: ≈0.25π is the sparse setting. π is a Clifford (no scrambling). θ and π−θ coincide only when theta_x = 0, not at the default drive, so the upper half of the range is its own territory. The sign is invisible unless theta_z > 0.
theta_zz.title: Theta Zz

twirls.description: ZZ-commutant Pauli twirls per circuit, averaged. Only useful on hardware: it randomises off-axis coherent error in the couplings. Multiplies the circuit count, so it multiplies QPU time.
twirls.title: Twirls

via.description: How to reach the machine. `direct`: this engine drives qiskit-ibm-runtime itself (analytic emulation, native fractional gates, one batched QPU session). `mothbackend`: route through Moth's execution service, which holds the credentials — sampled only, so no analytic mode, no fractional gates, and one submission per circuit.
via.title: Via

inputFiles.name: audio
inputFiles.description: Mono or stereo audio to process — WAV, MP3, OGG or FLAC. Stereo is summed to mono first, since the taps place their own stereo image. The file's own sample rate wins over the `sr` param.

inputFiles.name: ir
inputFiles.description: A previously measured impulse response — an otoc-echo `trajectory` envelope. Supply it to re-render without paying for the measurement again, and every echo param is ignored. Pass the asset id of a previous retrocausal-echo job's own `ir` output (output assets carry `slot` and `job_id`, so they chain straight into `input_files`), or upload the JSON yourself. `job:<id>/ir` is the documented alias for the same thing but may not resolve — prefer the asset id.

outputFiles.name: result
outputFiles.description: The primary output. With `emit: audio` (the default) this is the rendered stereo WAV. With `emit: map` no audio is rendered at all and this is the tap map as JSON — the same envelope the `taps` slot carries — so a sequencer or plugin can place the events itself without downloading audio.

outputFiles.name: ir
outputFiles.description: The impulse response actually used, as an otoc-echo `trajectory` envelope. Its output asset chains straight into another job's `input_files.ir` — one measurement, many mixes.

outputFiles.name: taps
outputFiles.description: The full `media` result envelope: provenance, the audio's shape, the echo summary, the spec, and the rendered tap map (time_ms, level, pan, F, polarity per tap). This is where a caller reads the numbers; a DAW or plugin can load it directly.

errorCodes.description: params fail Params' own field validation (type/range) or a cross-field check (square lattice without width/height, kick_site outside the line, shots over the cap without allow_high_shots).
the `ir` input is not UTF-8 JSON, or not an otoc-echo `trajectory` envelope. A bare envelope, a handler return wrapped in `output`, and a whole job result wrapped in `result` are all accepted.
the `audio` input could not be decoded as a PCM or float WAV, is over the size cap, or decoded to zero samples.
the input, or the input plus its computed tail, exceeds the render length cap. Set tail_ms explicitly or send a shorter file.
no tap survived min_level — the echo was fully erased at this theta_x, or min_level is too high. The echo summary is in the message.
the tap map is larger than the render cap. Raise min_level or lower depth.
the delay line needs more qubits than the machine allows — 24 for aer, the device's own width for an IBM backend. Supplying a measured `ir` sidesteps this entirely.
machine is neither 'aer' nor an IBM backend name the runtime knows.

the requested execution route could not be reached — for `via: direct`, qiskit-ibm-runtime is missing or no credentials were supplied (qpu_token param / QISKIT_IBM_TOKEN); for `via: mothbackend`, the mothbackend package is absent or the service returned a transport error. Retryable.
the estimator returned an error while running the echo circuits.

direction.description:
Which qubits receive the blur rotation, controlling the spatial direction of the blur effect:

- `full` — all pixel qubits are rotated, producing blur in both directions (default).
- `vertical` — only the y-encoding qubits are rotated; the blur spreads vertically.
- `horizontal` — only the x-encoding qubits are rotated; the blur spreads horizontally.
direction.title: Direction

downscale.description: If True, oversized regions are downscaled before teleport and upscaled back. If False, oversized regions are tiled into adjacent sub-images.
downscale.title: Downscale

mask_bin_size.description: Mask quantisation step as a percentage of 255 (0–100). Pixel values below this threshold are treated as background, preventing near-zero JPEG/WebP compression artifacts from being detected as separate mask regions. Default 4 (~10/255).
mask_bin_size.title: Mask Bin Size

mask_min_region.description: Minimum mask region size in pixels. Connected components smaller than this are discarded after quantisation, removing residual compression artifacts that survive the binning step. Default 16.
mask_min_region.title: Mask Min Region

size.description: Pixel budget per teleblur pass: a region up to `size × size` pixels is teleported in a single pass. Must be between 8 and 1024. Default 1024.
size.title: Size

strength.description: Strength of the teleportation effect, between 0.0 and 1.0
strength.title: Strength

inputFiles.name: image1
inputFiles.description: The source image. The teleblur effect morphs this image toward image2 through quantum rotation gates. Supported formats: PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, BMP.

inputFiles.name: image2
inputFiles.description: The target image. The teleblur effect morphs image1 toward this image. If the dimensions differ from image1, image2 is resized to match before processing.

inputFiles.name: mask
inputFiles.description:
Optional mask controlling where the effect is applied, on a per-pixel
basis. Must match the size of `image1`. Each output pixel is a soft
blend `C = m · C_teleblurred + (1 - m) · C_image1`, where `m` is the
normalised mask intensity at that pixel: black keeps image1, white takes
the fully teleblurred result, and grey values blend smoothly between the
two. Single-channel masks are used directly; RGB masks are converted to
luminance.

**Alpha-channel fallback**

If no mask is provided, the alpha channel of `image1` is used instead
(transparent pixels keep image1, opaque pixels are teleblurred). For
RGB input with no alpha channel, the whole image is teleblurred.

outputFiles.name: result
outputFiles.description: The processed image.

Good for flat-color/graphic-style images.

machine.description: Where to run the circuit. 'aer' is a noiseless local simulator. 'fake_<chip>' options (e.g. 'fake_fez', 'fake_sherbrooke', 'fake_torino') are local simulators calibrated to a real current IBM chip's noise. 'ibm_<chip>' options (e.g. 'ibm_fez', 'ibm_miami', 'ibm_marrakesh') submit to that real IBM Quantum hardware; 'least_busy' submits to whichever operational device currently has the shortest queue.

range_correction.title: Range Correction

separate_rgb.description: Give each of the three colour coordinates its own circuit. Turn this off to put the two angles on one circuit instead: a qubit is cos(theta/2)|0> + e^(i phi)|1>, so the sphere's polar angle can ride in the rotation and hue in the phase of the same cell, turning three circuits into two at the cost of a second measurement setting and a noisier reconstruction. Ignored when fixed_palette is set.
separate_rgb.title: Separate Rgb

shots.description: Number of measurement shots to sample, per processed field.
shots.title: Shots

inputFiles.name: image
inputFiles.description: The image to encode. By default every pixel becomes a point on the colour sphere -- a radius and two angles, the same coordinates that describe a qubit's own state -- and each of those three goes through the quantum encode/measure/decode round trip, any that doesn't vary passed through unencoded, before the image is recomposed. With fixed_palette the image is instead quantized to a palette of its own colours (capped at 256) and only the per-pixel palette index makes the trip. The alpha channel, if any, passes through unchanged.

outputFiles.name: result
outputFiles.description: The recomposed image after the quantum round trip.

distortion.title: Distortion

Set False only to isolate its effect for a controlled comparison; normal callers should leave this on. Ignored for mode='sim'/'emu' (no idle-time dephasing to counteract either way).
dynamical_decoupling.title: Dynamical Decoupling

Currently 'zne' (Zero-Noise Extrapolation) - genuine accuracy gain but runs the circuit at multiple noise-scaled variants, so real extra QPU time/cost. Opt-in only, never a silent default. Ignored for mode='sim'.
error_mitigation.title: Error Mitigation

fixed_palette.description: Import the image through a palette of its own colours (capped at 256) and run only the resulting per-pixel palette index through the device -- as exact, losslessly-quantized levels -- instead of decomposing it into the continuous colour-sphere coordinates. Good for flat-color/graphic-style images.

gate_pauli.description: Which two-qubit Pauli pair (P, Q) to use for the exp(i*distortion/2*(P⊗Q)) gate applied between adjacent data qubits in transform_channels, e.g. 'XY', 'ZZ'.
gate_pauli.title: Gate Pauli

max_tiles.description: Safety cap on mode='emu'/'qpu' tiling (see the module's own tiling docstring): an oversized image for a fixed-capacity chip is now split into tiles instead of downsampled away, and real cost scales with the NUMBER of tiles (each is its own extra circuit in the shared submission, so real extra queue time/cost on mode='qpu'), not with pixel count directly - nothing bounds that automatically. Rejected outright (before any circuit runs) when the image would need more tiles than this. Raise explicitly to accept a bigger job's cost/time; ignored for mode='sim' (no fixed capacity to tile against - it grows its own lattice to fit instead, up to topology._MAX_LATTICE_DIM).
max_tiles.title: Max Tiles

mode.description: 'sim' runs on a local noiseless simulator, sized to fit the image (no backend_name needed). 'emu' runs locally against a real IBM chip's own calibration snapshot via moth_backbone (needs an explicit backend_name, e.g. 'sherbrooke' - no 'fake_' prefix). 'qpu' submits to real hardware via moth_backbone.
mode.title: Mode

pole_clamp.description: How far each single-field channel's (r/theta, or index for fixed_palette) encoded angle stays from the poles (theta=0/pi). HISTORICAL NOTE, why this defaults to 0 now: this field predates iqpixl's own linear-in-<Z> encoding fix (see Mode.angles' own docstring) - the ORIGINAL rationale was that theta=arccos(<Z>)'s decode slope is infinite at the poles, amplifying shot/readout noise hardest at extreme values, and a nonzero clamp bounded that slope. Once the encoding itself was changed so <Z> is linear in the value (no arccos anywhere in the decode path), that slope-blowup no longer exists, and re-measuring (same noisy local simulation, same realistic ~2-3%/qubit readout error this field's own earlier measurement used) found NO consistent benefit from a nonzero clamp any more - error was flat within noise across 0 to 0.2*pi. Shot-noise variance is actually LOWEST at the poles under the new encoding (a Bloch-sphere qubit's own measurement variance is (1-<Z>^2)/shots, minimized at <Z>=+-1), so clamping away from them now trades away real signal for no compensating benefit. Left as a settable escape hatch (e.g. for a systematic, non-shot-noise effect like T1 decay during measurement, which a per-cell affine/readout calibration - see codec.calibrate_readout - already corrects for anyway) rather than removed outright, but 0 is now the default for every mode, sim included (a field pinned exactly to a pole is a deterministic |0>/|1> measurement with ZERO shot variance regardless of shot count on a noiseless simulator - confirmed directly: a flat/grayscale image's exact noiseless round trip depends on this staying 0 there). Applies to every single-field channel (r always; theta/phi too when separate_rgb=True) - never to the paired theta/phi circuit (separate_rgb=False), whose own theta already gets iqpixl's own pair-mode default (0.2*pi) automatically, nor to fixed_palette's index channel, which stays exact (clamp=0) on purpose - quant_levels='auto' there promises a lossless round trip, and clamping would break that promise.
pole_clamp.title: Pole Clamp

provider.description: Execution family for mode='qpu'/'emu' - 'ibm' | 'iqm'. Omit for a real IBM device name (inferred), or for mode='emu' to reach IBM's fake_<chip> catalog; set 'iqm' for mode='emu' to reach IQM's own fake_<chip> catalog instead, or for mode='qpu' to target IQM hardware.
provider.title: Provider

range_correction.description: Stretch each decoded field back over its original dynamic range. Off by default -- the raw decoded values are used as-is, with no correction.
range_correction.title: Range Correction

readout_calibration.description: Whether to measure and correct per-cell noise before decoding - iqpixl's own calibrate_affine: one real, GENERIC-data calibration circuit (same graph/mode/clamp as the real channels), fitting a per-cell affine <Z> gain/offset via least squares over that cell's own address configs. Its own circuits ride in the SAME combined submission as every channel this image decodes (see decode_channels) - not a separate batch, not once per channel or per cell. Corrects the real circuit's OWN accumulated gate error in addition to readout error (unlike a bare measurement-only calibration), because iqpixl's own linear-in-<Z> encoding (Mode.angles) makes a depolarizing-style contraction EXACTLY affine in the value. Confirmed empirically (noisy local simulation, realistic ~1%/qubit gate + ~2-3%/qubit readout error): mean reconstruction error dropped ~70% when enabled - confirm before assuming that figure holds at a different noise scale. Real, genuine extra cost (len(graph.groups) more circuits in the shared batch, at the same shots= as everything else) - opt-in, not a silent default, same reasoning as error_mitigation. KNOWN LIMITATION, not planned to change: the calibration circuits' shots are the SAME shots= as the real channels, with no independent knob - SubmitJobBatchRequest.shots is one value for the WHOLE batch by design (moth_backbone's own proto comment: a per-circuit override would silently split one real submission into several), and fixing that means either touching archaeo/moth_interconnect (out of scope) or giving calibration its own separate submission (a second real queue entry - exactly what batching this into one call exists to avoid). Low shots= can therefore under-shoot calibration's own stability - if that matters, use a higher shots= or leave this off. Ignored for mode='sim' (noiseless - the fit's own shot noise is then pure overhead with nothing to correct). With separate_rgb=False, the one paired theta/phi channel gets iqpixl's calibrate_readout (per-qubit confusion matrices) instead - calibrate_affine's own fit is tied to the clamp it was measured against, and that channel's own clamp differs from the other channels' (see decode_channels' own docstring). A fitted calibration is cached process-wide (keyed by backend/clamp/shots, with a TTL), so only the first image on a given backend/settings pays for it.
readout_calibration.title: Readout Calibration

separate_rgb.description: Give each of the three colour coordinates its own circuit. Turn this off to put the two angles on one circuit instead: a qubit is cos(theta/2)|0> + e^(i phi)|1>, so the sphere's polar angle can ride in the rotation and hue in the phase of the same cell, turning three circuits into two at the cost of a second measurement setting and a noisier reconstruction. Ignored when fixed_palette is set.
separate_rgb.title: Separate Rgb

shots.description: Base number of measurement shots to sample, per processed field. The ACTUAL submitted count scales with the graph's own worst-case cell degree (see decode_channels' own `_shots_for_graph`): every address config in a degree-d cell shares the SAME shot budget (one joint measurement setting reads all 2**d of them at once), so a higher-degree chip (e.g. IQM's square-lattice garnet) dilutes per-value precision more than a lower-degree one (e.g. IBM's heavy-hex fez) at the SAME nominal shots= - silently paying more error for the same setting. Scaled by 2**max_degree / 8 (degree 3 - the common heavy-hex case - is unchanged; higher-degree chips pay more shots, lower-degree ones fewer) so the same shots= means comparable per-value precision across backends, not the same literal circuit count.
shots.title: Shots

simulator.description: mode='sim' only - which local simulator moth_backbone executes circuits against. Defaults to 'aer'. 'pennylane_lightning' and 'cudaq_sim' are real, separate simulator backends (not aliases of aer) - useful to compare against aer's own time/fidelity, not just hardware's. Ignored for mode='emu'/'qpu'.
simulator.title: Simulator

twirling.description: Whether mode='qpu' submissions get Pauli twirling on two-qubit gates - randomizes each physical CX/ECR instance's Pauli frame so coherent gate errors average into a stochastic channel across shots, no extra circuit executions, so it's on by default (same reasoning as dynamical_decoupling). IBM-only - real, already-wired archaeo capability (sampler.options.twirling); silently has no effect for provider='iqm' (logged server-side, not an error). Ignored for mode='sim'/'emu' (no gate-level noise model to twirl either way).
twirling.title: Twirling

inputFiles.name: image
inputFiles.description: The image to encode. By default every pixel becomes a point on the colour sphere -- a radius and two angles, the same coordinates that describe a qubit's own state -- and each of those three goes through the quantum encode/measure/decode round trip, any that doesn't vary passed through unencoded, before the image is recomposed. With fixed_palette the image is instead quantized to a palette of its own colours (capped at 256) and only the per-pixel palette index makes the trip. The alpha channel, if any, passes through unchanged.

outputFiles.name: result
outputFiles.description: The recomposed image after the quantum round trip.

errorCodes.description: The image file could not be decoded.
distortion is greater than 0 on a machine that reads out per-group (every machine except real IBM hardware) -- the cross-cell gate it adds is silently dropped there, so it would have no effect.

mode='sim' only -- the image's pixel count exceeds the largest supported simulated lattice (64x64). "sim" sizes its own lattice to fit the image; this is what it hits instead once that growth runs out of room.

mode='sim' only -- the image's pixel count exceeds the data-qubit capacity of the largest lattice "sim" can grow to (see too_many_values). Not reachable for mode='emu'/'qpu', which tile an oversized image across a fixed-capacity chip instead (see too_many_tiles).

mode='emu'/'qpu' only -- the image needs more tiles than max_tiles allows to fit the selected machine's fixed data-qubit capacity. Each tile is a real backend submission, so this bounds real cost/time explicitly rather than tiling an arbitrarily large image for free; raise max_tiles to accept the extra cost, or shrink the image.
the requested machine name isn't recognized.
Could not authenticate/connect to IBM Quantum with the given token/instance.
The transpiled circuit was rejected or the sampling job failed to submit.
The output image could not be encoded.
